t:
(a) 
There is hereby established in the National Military Establishment a Munitions Board (hereinafter in this section referred to as the “Board”).
 
    (b) 
The Board shall be composed of a Chairman, who shall be the head thereof, and an Under Secretary or Assistant Secretary from each of the three military departments, to be designated in each case by the Secretaries of their respective departments. The Chairman shall be appointed from civilian life by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, and shall receive compensation at the rate of $14,000 a year.

 
    (c) It shall be the duty of the Board under the direction of the Secretary of Defense and in support of strategic and logistic plans prepared by the Joint Chiefs of Staff—

        (1) 
to coordinate the appropriate activities within the National Military Establishment with regard to industrial matters, including the procurement, production, and distribution plans of the departments and agencies comprising the Establishment;
 
        (2) 
to plan for the military aspects of industrial mobilization;
 
        (3) 
to recommend assignment of procurement responsibilities among the several military services and to plan for standardization of specifications and for the greatest practicable allocation of purchase authority of technical equipment and common use items on the basis of single procurement:
 
        (4) 
to prepare estimates of potential production, procurement, and personnel for use in evaluation of the logistic feasibility of strategic operations;
 
        (5) 
to determine relative priorities of the various segments of the military procurement programs;
 
        (6) 
to supervise such subordinate agencies as are or may be created to consider the subjects falling within the scope of the Board’s responsibilities;
 
        (7) 
to make recommendations to regroup, combine, or dissolve existing interservice agencies operating in the fields of procurement, production, and distribution in such manner as to promote efficiency and economy;
 
        (8) 
to maintain liaison with other departments and agencies for the proper correlation of military requirements with the civilian economy, particularly in regard to the procurement, or disposition of strategic and critical material and the maintenance of adequate reserves of such material, and to make recommendations as to policies in connection therewith;
 
        (9) 
to assemble and review material and personnel requirements presented by the Joint Chiefs of Staff and those presented by the production, procurement, and distribution agencies assigned to meet military needs, and to make recommendations thereon to the Secretary of Defense; and
 
        (10) 
to perform such other duties as the Secretary of Defense may direct.
  
    (d) When the Chairman of the Board first appointed has taken office, the Joint Army and Navy Munitions Board shall cease to exist and all its records and personnel shall be transferred to the Munitions Board.
 
    (e) The Secretary of Defense shall provide the Board with such personnel and facilities as the Secretary may determine to be required by the Board for the performance of its functions.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a Board whose Chairman is appointed "from civilian life" brings outsiders into federal decisions. But the Chairman is a salaried, Senate-confirmed federal officer, and the other members are Under or Assistant Secretaries of the military departments, so the Board sits entirely inside the federal government. Its duties, including liaison with "other departments and agencies," are intra-government coordination, with no public comment, hearing, outside advisory members, or right to sue.
fable.s: The Chairman shall be appointed from civilian life by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, and shall receive compensation at the rate of $14,000 a year.

qwen_block.w: The Munitions Board is composed entirely of federal officials: the Chairman is a presidential appointee receiving a salary, and the other members are Under Secretaries or Assistant Secretaries from the military departments. Although the Chairman is appointed from 'civilian life,' they become a high-ranking federal official upon appointment. There is no requirement for consultation with or participation by entities outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, or the general public) in the Board's decision-making process. The duties listed involve internal coordination within the National Military Establishment.
qwen_block.s: The Board shall be composed of a Chairman, who shall be the head thereof, and an Under Secretary or Assistant Secretary from each of the three military departments, to be designated in each case by the Secretaries of their respective departments. The Chairman shall be appointed from civilian life by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, and shall receive compensation at the rate of $14,000 a year.

opus.w: The Munitions Board is a federal agency made up entirely of federal officials: a salaried, Senate-confirmed Chairman and Under or Assistant Secretaries of the military departments. The phrase 'from civilian life' only describes where the Chairman comes from; once appointed, he is a federal employee doing his job, as with the NLRB board in Example 7. The Board's liaison and recommendation duties run to other federal departments, agencies and the Secretary of Defense, so all coordination stays inside the government.
opus.s: The Board shall be composed of a Chairman, who shall be the head thereof, and an Under Secretary or Assistant Secretary from each of the three military departments, to be designated in each case by the Secretaries of their respective departments. The Chairman shall be appointed from civilian life by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, and shall receive compensation at the rate of $14,000 a year.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning.** The tempting reading is "Yes." The Chairman is "appointed from civilian life," and the Board must "maintain liaison with other departments and agencies" on how military needs fit with the civilian economy. Both points fail the definition. The Chairman is confirmed by the Senate and paid a $14,000 salary, so once appointed he is a federal official. The other members are Under or Assistant Secretaries of the military departments. The liaison is only with other federal departments and agencies. No one outside the federal government takes part in any decision.

qwen_chat.w: The Munitions Board is composed entirely of federal officials (the Chairman and military department secretaries). Its duties involve internal coordination within the National Military Establishment and liaison with other federal departments and agencies. There is no requirement to consult or coordinate with entities outside the federal government, such as states, tribes, or the public.
qwen_chat.s: The Board shall be composed of a Chairman, who shall be the head thereof, and an Under Secretary or Assistant Secretary from each of the three military departments, to be designated in each case by the Secretaries of their respective departments.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Board's duty to "maintain liaison with other departments and agencies" or its role in coordinating activities implies participation with outside entities. However, the text explicitly limits the Board's composition to federal officials (the Chairman and Under/Assistant Secretaries from military departments) and its duties to internal coordination within the National Military Establishment. Liaison with "other departments and agencies" in this context refers to other federal entities, not outside parties like states, tribes, or the public. Furthermore, the Board is an internal federal agency, not an advisory committee with non-federal members.
